subject.title: fix(gateway): reject invalid session history limit with 400 instead of coercing to 1

question: Should the shipped session-history HTTP endpoint intentionally change malformed and below-one `limit` requests from a successful coerced response to HTTP 400?
rationale: The docs do not define malformed-query behavior, and the change can break callers relying on permissive coercion even though strict validation is cleaner.

options.title: Adopt strict validation
options.body: Fix the unsafe-integer gap, prove the real HTTP behavior, and intentionally accept the 200-to-400 compatibility change.

options.title: Preserve permissive behavior
options.body: Keep the shipped coercion contract and close this PR if compatibility outweighs strict input validation.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict validation
recommendation.body: Fix the unsafe-integer gap, prove the real HTTP behavior, and intentionally accept the 200-to-400 compatibility change.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the direct session-history HTTP/SSE endpoint and its original request contract.
